claims.text: The as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi films have an ordered, single-phase hexagonal structure.
The baseline FeMnNiGeSi films undergo a sharp first-order magnetostructural transition with pronounced hysteresis.
Lowering substrate temperature or increasing deposition rate will produce finer grains and a higher defect density in FeMnNiGeSi films.
Grain boundaries, dislocations, and stacking faults act as heterogeneous nucleation centers for the magnetostructural transition.
Increasing grain-boundary and defect density distributes the magnetostructural transition over a broader temperature range.
A high defect density produces a broader or more diffuse magnetic-entropy-change curve.
Defects can smear out an otherwise abrupt magnetic transition.
Broadening the transition through increased defect density reduces magnetic hysteresis.
Increasing grain-boundary or interface area improves thermal exchange.
Finer-grained FeMnNiGeSi films will have a broader ΔS(T) curve than standard as-deposited films.
Finer-grained FeMnNiGeSi films will have a smaller hysteresis-loop area during low-field cycling.
Finer-grained FeMnNiGeSi films will exhibit faster heat-exchange kinetics.
Broadening the transformation may slightly decrease the maximum amplitude of ΔS.
The baseline films have limited heat exchange because their grain-boundary or interface density is relatively low.
The predicted effects should apply near the magnetostructural transition under low applied magnetic fields.
Secondary-phase formation, loss of mechanical stability, or composition changes would place the films outside the proposed mechanism's domain.
Extreme deposition conditions may introduce compositional inhomogeneity or secondary phases that confound the microstructural effect.
